frames.narration: Orders are keyed by customer. Every order for ada goes to the same instance (Counter A), which keeps count[ada] in a local state store. At offset 300 ada has 41 orders.
Every 50 events the coordinator starts checkpoint 6. The source notes its offset (300) and inserts barrier 6 into the stream. Nothing is paused.
The barrier flows with the data. When it reaches an operator, that operator has seen exactly the events before offset 300, so its state is a consistent cut.
Each operator copies its state to durable storage (asynchronously, incrementally with RocksDB) and forwards the barrier. The sink closes its transaction for events up to 300 and waits.
All acknowledgements are in: checkpoint 6 is complete, holding all state plus offset 300 as one unit. Only now does the transactional sink commit the outputs up to offset 300.
The stream keeps going. Offsets 301 to 330 raise ada to 44, and their outputs sit in an open transaction. Then Counter B crashes and its memory is gone.
Recovery: the job restarts, every operator reloads checkpoint 6 (ada back to 41), the source rewinds to offset 300, and the sink aborts its open transaction.

The 30 events since the checkpoint are replayed. ada reaches 44 again, exactly once in the state. A plain sink would now see those 30 outputs twice; the transactional sink writes them once and commits at checkpoint 7.
